clue.text: Entire UN health authority supported by the French

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of, and so is supported by, the second

parts.note: the World Health Organization, the United Nations health body, is abbreviated WHO
le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Every bit of a UN health body is propped up by France.
explanation.definitionFit: Something entire is complete, with no part missing.

clue.text: When early man escaped from the Arctic eagerly

indicators.note: the answer's letters get out from inside the run of words that follows, spanning two of them

explanation.surface: Prehistoric people fled the frozen north as fast as they could.
explanation.definitionFit: The glacial period of prehistory is the era when early humans lived, so it can be clued as a time.

clue.text: What motorists step on to finish off with breathless speed?

definitions.text: What motorists step on to finish off with breathless speed?

parts.words: What motorists step on to finish off with breathless speed?
parts.note: drivers press the accelerator pedal for speed, and to strangle someone, finishing them off by cutting off breath, is the same word as a verb

explanation.surface: A question about what drivers press to race to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one question about racing, but it hides two senses: the engine's speed control and the verb for choking someone to death.
explanation.definitionFit: The pedal controlling engine speed and the act of strangling share one word.

clue.text: Hand me down-the mooring lines apparently

definitions.meaning: a hand-me-down is a discarded garment passed on to someone else
to release the ropes holding a boat to the quay is the sailing phrase for setting off

explanation.surface: A request on board to pass down the ropes that tie up the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A discarded garment is a reject, and releasing a boat's ropes is the sailing command to leave.

clue.text: 48 inches on which cats proverbially manage to land

definitions.meaning: twelve inches make a foot, so 48 inches is a measure of four of them

definitions.text: on which cats proverbially manage to land
definitions.meaning: the saying goes that a cat dropped from a height always lands on all its paws

explanation.surface: A height of four feet from which cats famously land unhurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty-eight inches is a length in imperial units, and a cat's four paws are what it proverbially lands on.

clue.text: Sociable type must be a reliable cocktail maker

definitions.meaning: a person who gets along easily with strangers at parties
a barman who blends drinks well, or a dependable shaker

explanation.surface: A friendly person needs to be able to shake a decent drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at ease in company is called this, and a skilled blender of drinks earns the same phrase literally.

clue.text: A fool one has to suffer the morning after?

definitions.meaning: a dim, stupid person

definitions.text: one has to suffer the morning after?
definitions.meaning: the aching, foggy skull of a hangover after a night of drinking

explanation.surface: Being an idiot is something you pay for the next day.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is called this, and a hangover leaves a person with a heavy, dull skull.

clue.text: Succeeded at one's first riding lesson

definitions.meaning: made progress, prospered
the first thing a novice rider does is climb onto the horse

explanation.surface: Doing well at a first lesson in horse riding.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to make headway in life, and a beginner rider's first achievement is mounting the horse.

clue.text: Mountain ridge a rider applies to mount

definitions.meaning: a projecting ridge running out from a mountain range
a horseman presses a spiked heel device against his horse, the mount, to urge it on

explanation.surface: A rider tackles a mountain ridge on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' looks like climbing onto the horse, but it is the horse itself, to which the rider applies the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge jutting from a mountain and the spiked heel goad used by riders share one name.

clue.text: Leave the other fellow penniless and scram

definitions.meaning: to strip someone of all their money, as at cards
slang for go away quickly

explanation.surface: Fleece the other man of his cash and then run off.
explanation.definitionFit: To empty someone of their money and to leave in a hurry share the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Pray do rewrite a skit

indicators.note: the letters of the two words before are written again in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to rework a comic sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic imitation mocking something, a send-up.

clue.text: A prelimary contest will raise the temperature

definitions.meaning: a qualifying round of a race, the printed 'prelimary' being a slip for preliminary
warmth, which makes things hotter

explanation.surface: An early round of competition gets everyone hot under the collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualifying round in athletics carries this name, and warmth is what raises temperature.

clue.text: Not to worry if you make money illegally and get the bird

parts.note: to counterfeit banknotes or coins is to forge them
the tit is a small common songbird

explanation.surface: Don't fret about counterfeiting cash and being jeered off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the bird' looks like the idiom for being booed; here the bird is simply a tit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissive phrase telling someone to drop the matter, never mind.

clue.text: Remove name from register if industrial action is cancelled

definitions.meaning: to delete someone, such as a struck-off doctor, from an official list
a workers' walkout that has been called off

explanation.surface: A union member is deleted from the books if the walkout is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: Deleting a name from a professional roll and a called-off walkout share the phrase.

clue.text: A really difficult question for a rotten egg

definitions.meaning: a fiendishly hard problem, such as an exam question
a nasty, unpleasant person, or literally something that smells foul

explanation.surface: A hard question put to a nasty piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A brutally hard problem and a contemptible person are both given this slang name.

clue.text: Boxing titled paintings

parts.note: someone with a title, such as a lord, is a noble

explanation.surface: Pictures of aristocrats are put into crates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' suggests packing, but it is the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Pugilism has long been nicknamed the gentlemanly sport of fighting with fists.

clue.text: He keeps an eye out for the originator of gamesmanship

definitions.meaning: a lookout or observer, such as a birdwatcher
Stephen Potter wrote the humorous book Gamesmanship

explanation.surface: A lookout for the man who invented winning by gamesmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Potter (1900-69) was a British humorist whose book The Theory and Practice of Gamesmanship coined the word; his initial and surname run together.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer watching for planes, birds or talent has this name, as does Stephen Potter written with his initial.

clue.text: Identification code needed to transmit news

parts.note: to pass something on is to hand or send it
word is information, as in 'any word from him?'

explanation.surface: A secret code is required to send out information.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret term given to prove identity before being admitted.

clue.text: How a straightedge is employed usually

definitions.meaning: a straightedge is used in the role of a ruler for drawing lines
generally, in most cases

explanation.surface: How a straightedge is normally used.
explanation.definitionFit: A straightedge serves in the role of a ruler, and the same phrase means generally or normally.

clue.text: Base diet should be planned sugar-free!

definitions.text: Base diet should be planned sugar-free!

indicators.note: the two words before are to be arranged anew, worked out in a different order

explanation.surface: A dietary instruction that a basic eating plan should cut out sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the shuffled words give the condition, and the clue describes how it is managed, with a basic diet free of sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: The disease in which the body cannot regulate blood glucose is managed by a planned diet low in sugar.

clue.text: Quarrel as yet unfinished

definitions.meaning: a fuss or commotion, a row
still awaiting completion, like a task on a list

explanation.surface: An argument that has not yet been settled.
explanation.definitionFit: A row or fuss is a hyphenated noun, and the same two short words describe a task still pending.

clue.text: Blow on the foot to keep it warm

definitions.meaning: a punch, as in '... him on the jaw'

definitions.text: on the foot to keep it warm
definitions.meaning: a knitted covering worn on the foot inside a shoe

explanation.surface: A kick to the foot, followed by advice to keep it warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard punch and a woollen foot covering share one word.

clue.text: First rate selection

definitions.meaning: of high quality, as in a fine cut of meat
a pick from alternatives

explanation.surface: A top-quality range to pick from.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-grade goods and a pick from options share the word.

clue.text: Readjust rates and rents

indicators.note: the word that follows is to have its letters adjusted into a new order

explanation.surface: A landlord changes charges and rental fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rents' looks like payments to a landlord, but it is the noun for rips.
explanation.definitionFit: Rents are rips or splits in cloth.

clue.text: Nymph gets deer in trouble

indicators.note: the two words before are in disorder, stirred up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sea spirit gets a deer into difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the daughters of Nereus were sea nymphs.

clue.text: Uncooked, filleted, and lean

parts.note: a filleted fish has had its bones taken out

explanation.surface: A fish served raw, filleted and with little fat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a list of food descriptions; only the last word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaunt, bony person with little flesh is described as lean.

clue.text: What an otherwise cold man approaches withenthusiasm

definitions.text: What an otherwise cold man approaches
definitions.meaning: a chilly person draws close to a burning hearth, read as two words, a blaze
ablaze with zeal, burning keenly; the print runs 'with enthusiasm' together

explanation.surface: A chilly man warms to things with real keenness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ablaze with passion is to burn with eagerness, and a freezing man heads for a hearth's flames.

clue.text: The previous best 78?

definitions.meaning: the best performance or time before the latest one was set
a 78 is an old gramophone disc played at 78 revolutions per minute

explanation.surface: A question about a former top score expressed as a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A previous best time is a superseded mark, and a 78 rpm disc is a vintage piece of vinyl's forerunner.
